guide.title: Farmer guide
guide.intro: Short lessons on reading prices and the outlook.
guide.prices.title: Modal, lowest and highest price
guide.prices.p1: Each market report gives three prices for one quintal (100 kg).
guide.prices.p2: The lowest and highest are the smallest and biggest prices paid that day. The modal price is the price paid most often. Use it as the normal price.
guide.prices.p3: Example: tomato in Kolar. Lowest ₹800, highest ₹1,400, modal ₹1,100. Most farmers got about ₹1,100 per quintal.
guide.trends.title: Price trends
guide.trends.p1: A trend shows how the price moved in the last 30 days: rising, falling or steady.
guide.trends.p2: Price swings show how much the price jumps from day to day. Big swings mean more risk.
guide.trends.p3: A trend is about the past. It does not promise that the price will keep moving the same way.
guide.forecasts.title: Reading a forecast
guide.forecasts.p1: A forecast gives a middle estimate and a range for the next report, and for 3, 7 and 14 days ahead.
guide.forecasts.p2: The middle estimate is the single most likely number. The range shows where the price will probably be.
guide.forecasts.p3: Example: onion in Lasalgaon, last price ₹1,500. In 7 days: middle estimate ₹1,580, range ₹1,350 to ₹1,800.
guide.wrong.title: Why forecasts can be wrong
guide.wrong.p1: Rain, festivals, transport strikes, government decisions and large arrivals from other states can change prices suddenly.
guide.wrong.p2: The model learns only from past market reports. It cannot know about these events.
guide.wrong.p3: The app shows how wrong the forecast was in past tests, so you know how much to trust it.
guide.ranges.title: Uncertainty ranges
guide.ranges.p1: In past tests, the 80% range held the real price about 8 times out of 10. The 90% range is wider and held it about 9 times out of 10.
guide.ranges.p2: So sometimes the real price falls outside the range.
guide.ranges.p3: A wide range means the forecast is unsure. Be careful with big decisions.
guide.compare.title: Comparing markets
guide.compare.p1: The same crop can get different prices in nearby markets on the same day.
guide.compare.p2: Compare only recent reports. A price from a week ago is not a fair comparison, so it is marked “older report”.
guide.compare.p3: Example: tomato ₹1,100 in Kolar and ₹1,250 in Chintamani. Subtract your transport cost before you decide.
guide.transport.title: Transport and storage costs
guide.transport.p1: Moving produce costs money: vehicle, loading, commission and market fees.
guide.transport.p2: Storing produce also costs money. Tomato, leafy vegetables and fruit lose quality fast. Grains and pulses keep longer.
guide.transport.p3: Enter your own costs in the outlook card. The outlook is worked out again with your numbers.
guide.signals.title: Using SELL, HOLD, WATCH and COMPARE
guide.signals.p1: SELL: even the higher estimate is not above the last price. Selling now may be worth considering.
guide.signals.p2: HOLD: even the lower estimate is above the last price plus storage costs. WATCH: there is no clear signal.
guide.signals.p3: COMPARE: a nearby market recently reported a clearly higher price. Check it before you travel.
guide.guarantee.title: No guarantee of future price
guide.guarantee.p1: These signals are a market outlook. They are not a promise and not financial advice.
guide.guarantee.p2: The app does not know your costs, your crop quality or your need for cash.
guide.guarantee.p3: Use the outlook as one input. Also talk to traders, your FPO or the agriculture extension officer.
guide.missing.title: When data is missing or old
guide.missing.p1: Some markets do not report every day. Then the latest price can be several days old.
guide.missing.p2: Always look at the report date. If it is more than 3 days old, the app shows a warning.
guide.missing.p3: If your market has no recent report, look at nearby markets or call the market office (APMC).
